ClaimText: - CLM-005 — ADR-014 is preserved as historical evidence of the frozen v0.4 application. Its archived text allocated deterministic acts, RBAC, reporting, human-only acts, visibility, and data boundaries to a PEC project adapter, but that allocation is **not** a live carried posture for PEC v2: D-PEC-58 expressly states that the equivalent D-PEC-56 adapter-retention behavior did not survive retirement of the old product. The live carried boundary is limited to Root ownership of generic runtime semantics, PEC as an optional client with no second execution loop, and the surviving human-only-act restrictions. Sources: `projects/pec/docs/.archive/adr/ADR.md` §ADR-014; `execution/_Coordination/_DECISIONS/D-PEC-58_prd_v2_adoption.md`; `docs/PRD.md` §15.
AcceptedSourceRefs: PRD v2.2 §13/§15; D-PEC-67 L-A2; SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md rev1.3 SOW-088; SCA-003
Notes: Direct proof clause: explicitly rejects the retired ADR-014 PEC-project-adapter allocation and limits carry-forward to the accepted v2 boundary.

ClaimText: - CLM-006 — The recorded basis for the core-isolation decision is the Gate 4 exchange captured in `SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md` §Open Issues, row OI-012: the PRD invariants force the isolation properties under either candidate style (PEC-K-07 makes bridges disposable inputs; PEC-K-02 makes the store a throwaway projection; PEC-SVC-001 is the dependency-free-core rule); the package partition is congruent with a hexagonal grain (core: PKG-03/04/05 plus PKG-01 entities; driven edges: PKG-02/06 plus store; driving edges: PKG-07/08/09); nearly all §16 open decisions are adapter-level, so core isolation keeps them open cheaply; the lighter functional-core/imperative-shell variant fits a deterministic-derivation service with less ceremony; the one seam to keep crisp is entity schema (core) versus store persistence (adapter) inside PKG-01.

Section: Deliverable Definition — Ontology / Subject matter carried into the outputs
